payload.title: Bag-out stops after sorting with AGV or robot sequence disruption
payload.user_facing_summary: Use this flow when the site reports that bag-out will not complete after sorting, manual bagging is required, or AGVs/robots appear out of sequence or inactive. The troubleshooting goal is to determine whether the stoppage aligns with AGV inactivity or exchange-pair/sequence disruption and then perform approved fleet recovery and validation.
payload.playbook_goal: Restore bag-out operation by confirming whether AGV/robot inactivity or sequence disruption is blocking the process and guiding approved fleet recovery and validation.
observed_entry_symptoms: System stops at bag-out after sorting.
Bag-out starts and then stops before completion.
Site is manually bagging out.
Site suspects a robot or AGV is out of sequence or position.
An AGV appears not to have moved for an extended period.
payload.confidence_reason: The source strongly supports the symptom pattern and several troubleshooting directions, including AGV inactivity review, remove/add pair attempts, and validation when robots returned to proper sequence. Confidence is reduced because the exact decisive recovery path is not fully isolated and some details are OCR-garbled.

nodes.title: Confirm the bag-out stoppage matches the AGV or robot disruption pattern
nodes.intent: Determine whether the reported issue is a bag-out-after-sorting stoppage with manual bagging, incomplete bag-out progress, or site-reported AGV/robot sequence concerns rather than a different production issue.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the reported issue is a bag-out-after-sorting stoppage with manual bagging, incomplete bag-out progress, or site-reported AGV/robot sequence concerns rather than a different production issue.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to confirm the reported bag-out symptom pattern with the site, including whether bag-out stops after sorting, whether manual bagging is underway, whether the stoppage began after AGV removal or replacement activity, and whether the site is reporting a robot or AGV out of sequence or position.
nodes.source_supported_description: The case subject and multiple messages describe bag-out stopping after sorting, manual bagging, and site suspicion of robot or exchange-pair issues.

linked_runbooks.title: Recover an AGV That Lost a Tote Without Faulting
linked_runbooks.summary: Restore an AGV and tote to service after an AGV loses a tote without faulting by stopping RMS, manually moving the AGV to the Hospital, removing and re-adding the AGV at the Hospital station PC, power cycling the AGV, positioning it over the QR code in front of the Inbound Hospital Station, and removing and re-adding the missing tote so the AGV can return the tote to the sorter.
linked_runbooks.when_to_use: Use when an AGV has lost a tote without faulting and must be restored to service through the Hospital workflow described in section 5.8.2.6.
not_for: Do not use when the AGV is faulted; the packet references separate faulted-AGV recovery content.
Do not use when the missing tote cannot be removed or added back using the documented tote procedures.
Do not use when the AGV cannot be physically moved to the Hospital or cannot be re-added through the Hospital station PC.

responsibilities: E-stop RMS.
Use the AGV brake release and manually move the AGV to the Hospital.
Remove and re-add the AGV at the Hospital station PC/Hospital HMI.
Power cycle the AGV and verify the AGV lights turn green.
Position the AGV over the QR code in front of the Inbound Hospital Station.
Locate the missing tote and complete tote removal and add-back using the documented procedures.

safety_notes: This procedure is not marked support-safe in the candidate.
The procedure includes E-stop use, brake release use, manual AGV movement, and AGV power cycling.
Only maintenance or a supervisor should remove an AGV from the system, per the Add/Remove AGV source reference attached to the Hospital HMI screen artifact.

linked_runbooks.when_to_use: Use when an AGV has lost a tote without faulting and must be restored to service through the Hospital workflow described in section 5.8.2.6.
not_for: Do not use when the AGV is faulted; the packet references separate faulted-AGV recovery content.
Do not use when the missing tote cannot be removed or added back using the documented tote procedures.
Do not use when the AGV cannot be physically moved to the Hospital or cannot be re-added through the Hospital station PC.

responsibilities: E-stop RMS.
Use the AGV brake release and manually move the AGV to the Hospital.
Remove and re-add the AGV at the Hospital station PC/Hospital HMI.
Power cycle the AGV and verify the AGV lights turn green.
Position the AGV over the QR code in front of the Inbound Hospital Station.
Locate the missing tote and complete tote removal and add-back using the documented procedures.

safety_notes: This procedure is not marked support-safe in the candidate.
The procedure includes E-stop use, brake release use, manual AGV movement, and AGV power cycling.
Only maintenance or a supervisor should remove an AGV from the system, per the Add/Remove AGV source reference attached to the Hospital HMI screen artifact.

linked_runbooks.when_to_use: Use this procedure when a tote has been sent to the hospital station and the operator needs to confirm tote presence and determine why the tote was brought there for manual handling.
not_for: Do not use this runbook to interpret scanner codes, status values, or HMI fields beyond determining the reason, because the source does not provide those details.

payload.title: Hospital flow blocked by AGV or tote state inconsistency
payload.user_facing_summary: Use this candidate when the site reports that hospital flow is blocked by abnormal AGV placement, a disconnected tote still in the system, or robots needing removal and re-add after the primary issue. The flow focuses on confirming the AGV/tote inconsistency pattern in fleet or layout views, performing approved AGV/tote cleanup procedures, and validating that robots are back up and the system is moving again.
payload.playbook_goal: Restore movement and normal hospital-related flow by correcting AGV/tote state inconsistencies and abnormal AGV placement.
observed_entry_symptoms: AGV does not belong in the shown location

Disconnected tote remains in the system
Hospital is backed up while AGVs are picking tasks from abnormal positions
Robots need to be taken out and later re-added to restore operation
payload.confidence_reason: The packet strongly supports the existence of a distinct AGV/tote cleanup flow with abnormal AGV placement, disconnected tote records, AGV removal/re-add, and later recovery. Confidence is limited because the exact tools and exact approved cleanup procedures are only partially named and some evidence is chat-based or low-detail screenshots.

nodes.expected_or_observed_result: Escalation is required when the responder cannot safely continue, the suspected roster or mapping issue cannot be confirmed, or the system does not stabilize after the supported action path.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Use this gate only if the supported RMS-centered path is exhausted, unsafe, unauthorized, or unsuccessful.
